question.text: This empire located in the Indian subcontinent was founded by Babur. Shah Jahan who built the Taj Mahal, was a ruler of this empire.
question.clue: One ruler of this empire created a religion known as Din-e-ilahi.

swap.text: When she declared a state of emergency, Indira Gandhi and her son Sanjay spearheaded a population control strategy in which poor men and women were forced to undergo this medical procedure.
swap.answerHtml: sexual sterilization (accept word forms like sterilize; accept male and/or female sterilization; accept vasectomy or tubectomy)

question.text: After he murdered Mahatma Gandhi, Godse was put on trial in the Red Fort of this Indian city. A "New" district of this city is the capital of India.
question.clue: Plans for George VI to impress the "native minds" of this city by traveling to it via plane to hold a grand ceremony at Coronation Park were dropped because of their lack of political or financial tact.

swap.leadin: This man achieved his goals using satyagraha, or the force of truth.
swap.text: Name this leader who advocated nonviolence to help India achieve independence. In 1948, he was assassinated by Nathuram Godse.
swap.clue: This this man led a March to Dandi which led to a declaration of Pura Swaraj, or complete self-rule.

question.leadin: This country's fortress of Sigiriya was built by the king Kassapa.
question.text: Name this country that was home to the kingdoms of Polonnaruwa ("poh-luhn-uh-ROOV-uh") and Kandy. The Fourth Buddhist council was held in this country during the Anuradhapura ("uh-NOOR-uh-duh-POOR-uh") period.
question.answerHtml: Sri Lanka [or Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka]
question.clue: A rebel group in this country made up of members from that ethnicity bombed a temple containing the Buddha's tooth, dating to this country's kingdom of Kandy.

swap.text: The East India Company army was led by this man, who assumed command of the Company army following his unsuccessful bid for a seat in the House of Commons.
swap.clue: The definitive biography of this man is H.H. Dodwell's, which contrasts him to his French counterpart, Joseph Dupleix.

question.text: The Bofors scandal led to the downfall of an Indian politician with this surname. Other people with this surname included Indira and the leader of the Indian independence movement, Mahatma.
question.answerHtml: Gandhi (accept Rajiv Gandhi or Indira Gandhi or Mahatma Gandhi)
question.clue: Another leader with this surname resolved some tension with a western neighbor in the 1972 Shimla Agreement and was opposed by the Janata Party.

swap.leadin: This Indian leader is reputed to have built a terrible prison with the "facade of a spectacular palace."
swap.text: Name this son of Bindusara who was famous for his Rock Edicts. This man converted to Buddhism after realizing the atrocities he had committed during his conquest of Kalinga.
swap.clue: Some monuments created by this man were inscribed in Brahmi, others were inscribed in Greek.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about the current India-Pakistan conflict.
question.text: Discussions have been ongoing between Indian prime minister Atal Behari Vajpayee and this man, the Pakistani president since he overthrew Nawaz Sharif.
question.clue: This man was the chief architect of the Kargil plan, which was continually rejected by his superiors. After a military coup, he became the tenth president of Pakistan from 2001 to 2008.

swap.text: He resigned from the Imperial Legislative Council in protest against the Rowlatt Act and negotiated the Luchnow Pact. For 15 points, name this longtime leader of the Muslim League who became the founder of Pakistan.
swap.clue: This man declared a "Day of Deliverance" when, in protest of their country's entry into World War II, members of the Congress Party resigned from government.

question.leadin: This empire's ruler Rajaraja the Great built the Brihadisvara temple, dedicated to Shiva.
question.text: Rajaraja the Great ruled this empire which extended influence over much of the eastern Indian Ocean. Rajaraja and his successor Rajendra led this empire during its successful invasions of Sri Lanka and the Srivijaya kingdom.
question.clue: This empire's defeat of the Sailendra dynasty in Palembang was chronicled in inscriptions at the Brihadishvara Temple in this empire's capital of Thanjavur.

swap.leadin: Identify these events from the British colonization of India.
swap.text: Cartridges of Enfield Rifles greased with pork fat incited this uprising in 1857, which began in Meerut after the Bahadur Shah was proclaimed emperor and was put down by Colin Campbell.
swap.clue: This event saw the death of Henry Lawrence in the Siege of Lucknow.

question.text: This colony provided much of the manpower for Britain's attack on German East Africa, comprising the majority of the forces in the early battles of Kilimanjaro and Tanga. After the war, forces largely drawn from this colony fought in the Third Anglo-Afghan War.
question.clue: Lord Curzon established this colony's North-West Frontier Province, whose western border was set at the Durand Line to settle the Great Game with Russia.

swap.text: The Rocket Corps were developed by Hyder Ali and this king, also called the Tiger of Mysore, who fought the future Duke of Wellington in a series of four wars with British colonizers.
swap.clue: The V&A owns a wooden automaton commissioned by this man of a creature biting into the neck of a Western soldier.

question.leadin: This man brought a concealed dagger, a tiger claw and a suit of armour to a sword duel with Afzal Khan, and escaped from captivity dressed as a sweet carrier.
question.text: Name this founder and first Chhatrapati [Ch'hat-ruh-puhti] of the Maratha Confederacy, who carved a realm out in the areas around Bijapur.
question.clue: That general, Afzal Khan, was the subordinate of Sultan Ali Adil Shah of the Bijapur region, where this man engaged in guerrilla warfare.

swap.text: One of the earliest powerful Habshi was Jamal ud-Din Yaqut, an advisor and possible lover of the only female ruler of this state, Razia Sultan. Mohammed of Ghor founded this state.
swap.clue: This polity's ruling dynasties included the Burji and Khilji, and rulers of this polity including Balban were former slave soldiers known as ghulams.

question.leadin: This sultanate was usurped by the Hindu banker Raja Ganesha, who made a deal with Muslim nobles that his son would convert to Islam and succeed him as Jalal al-Din.
question.text: Name this sultanate founded by Ilyas Shah, who moved the capital to Pandua and remained largely independent of Delhi. This late medieval sultanate expanded the trade of its lands' renowned muslin.

swap.text: The famine also hit this historical region, where earlier events included the Battle of Seringapatam and British campaigns against Hyder Ali and Tippu Sultan.
swap.clue: This kingdom's last sultan successfully used rockets with attached blades in the Battle of Pollilur but died in 1799 while defending Seringapatam.

question.text: This woman, the subject of a 520-episode docudrama on Zee TV, was a widow of Gangadhar Rao who particularly hated the Doctrine of Lapse. She rounded up an army to reclaim her annexed kingdom during the 1857 Rebellion and led a big fight, but was defeated by the Central India Force led by Hugh Rose.
question.clue: Among the rulers of the princely states active after the fall of Maratha was this queen who died fighting the British at Gwalior Fort. Subhas Chandra Bose named his all-women regiment of the Indian National Army for this queen.

swap.leadin: During one of these wars Sir Eyre Coote repeatedly beat the forces of Hyder Ali.
swap.text: Name these wars, one of which was ended by the Treaty of Mangalore. During the fourth of these wars, the forces of Tipu Sultan used rockets with propellant held in iron tubes.
swap.clue: The second, which lasted from 1780-17884, was ended by the Treaty of Mangalore, and saw the defeat of Hyder Ali at Porto Nova and his subsequent death, leaving his kingdom to his son Tipu Sultan, who fought against Cornwallis.
